newsitem.title: USA: Clinton appeals for support at fundraiser.
newsitem.headline: Clinton appeals for support at fundraiser.

text.p: President Clinton told a group of Democratic donors at a fundraiser Wednesday that their support was critical to keep the country moving in the right direction.
"All we have to do is stay on the good issue, walk on the high road, and be able to find good candidates and finances and we can keep moving this country forward," he said.

The President spoke at a $2,500-a-plate Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee dinner expected to raise $1.5 million to retire last year's campaign debt and to fund Democratic senate candidates in the 1998 race.

The president cited the economic gains of the past four years and the balanced budget deal reached with congressional Republicans as the fruits of Democratic labour, leading to better lives for average Americans.

"What you do makes a difference in the lives of people you will never meet, you will never know and who could never afford to be here tonight," he told his well-heeled audience. "That is a unique role you occupy in American democracy."

The fundraiser was held at the Corcoran Gallery of Art, and the president and donors ate their dinners of sea bass and veal under the huge blown glass hanging sculptures of artist Dale Chihuly, who was in the audience.

The event was the second in a series of fundraisers the President will attend to help his fellow Democrats in the next election. In 1998, 18 Democratic and 16 Republican seats will be contested. The Republicans now control both chambers of Congress.
